title: Archaeological Works
summary: Prescribes the standard combination of headings for works on the archaeology of a place: the site name, [place]--Antiquities (or a qualified --Antiquities, Roman etc.), Antiquities, Prehistoric--[place], the people/culture/period, and Excavations (Archaeology)--[place]. Only six adjectival qualifiers are allowed after --Antiquities. Neither Antiquities, Prehistoric nor Excavations (Archaeology) is divided by individual site names; --Catalogs is not used under peoples. Also gives rules for establishing site names (add "Site", geographic qualifier, BT [modern country]--Antiquities).
validation_rules: Works on the archaeology of a place take a combination of: the site name (651) if about a specific site; `[place]--Antiquities` (or a qualified form); `Antiquities, Prehistoric--[place]`; the name of the people, prehistoric culture or period; and `Excavations (Archaeology)--[place]`. (H 1225 sec. D)

Headings for other special topics (pottery, burial sites, agriculture, etc.) are divided by place, including the name of the site if the work is about an individual site, e.g. `Tombs--Italy--Tarquinia`, `Iron age--England--Danebury Site`. (H 1225 sec. D)
`[place]--Antiquities` is valid under names of places, e.g. `Africa--Antiquities`, `France--Antiquities`, `London (England)--Antiquities`. (H 1225 sec. D.2)

For a work on a specific site, assign `[place]--Antiquities` only to bring out a locality below the level of a country (below the first-order political division for the United States, Great Britain, and Canada). (H 1225 sec. D.2)

The only qualified forms allowed are `--Antiquities, Byzantine`, `--Antiquities, Celtic`, `--Antiquities, Germanic`, `--Antiquities, Phoenician`, `--Antiquities, Roman`, `--Antiquities, Slavic`, and `--Antiquities, Turkish`; in all other cases use `--Antiquities` with no adjectival qualifier (e.g. not `--Antiquities, Etruscan`). (H 1225 sec. D.2)
For prehistoric antiquities use `Antiquities, Prehistoric--[place]`; do not divide this heading by names of individual sites. (H 1225 sec. D.2)

Assign a heading for the people who occupied the site, or the prehistoric culture or period, subdivided geographically if appropriate (e.g. `Neanderthals--France--Poitou-Charentes`). (H 1225 sec. D.3)
Under headings for extant peoples, use the subdivision --Antiquities, e.g. `Mayas--Antiquities`, `Pueblo Indians--Antiquities`. (H 1225 sec. D.3)
Assign the people heading even when --Antiquities is qualified by the corresponding ethnic adjective, e.g. `Romania--Antiquities, Celtic` plus `Celts--Romania`. (H 1225 sec. D.3)
Exception: do not assign `Romans` if `Italy--Antiquities, Roman` or `[locality within Italy]--Antiquities, Roman` has been assigned. (H 1225 sec. D.3)

Do not assign the people heading when the place in `[place]--Antiquities` corresponds exactly to the people (Greece/Greeks, Egypt/Egyptians, Gaul/Gauls, Hawaii/Hawaiians, Rome/Romans). (H 1225 sec. D.3)
If more than two peoples/cultures/periods, or none identifiable, the people heading may be omitted; for two, assign both. (H 1225 sec. D.3)
Use `Excavations (Archaeology)--[place]` for works about excavations in the place; do not divide this heading by names of individual sites. (H 1225 sec. D.4)
--Catalogs (free-floating form) may be used under names of individual sites, `[place]--Antiquities`, and `Excavations (Archaeology)--[place]` for works listing objects found. (H 1225 sec. E)
Do not use --Catalogs under headings for peoples: use `Rome--Antiquities--Catalogs`, not `Romans--Catalogs`. (H 1225 sec. E)

[LC practice] LC no longer uses form subdivisions; assign LCGFT (e.g. `Catalogs`) when a list of objects is more than 20% of the resource, and LCDGT where a demographic form subdivision would have been used. (H 1225 sec. A, E)

Establish site names per H 690; for obscure sites take the name from the work, add the word "Site" unless the name already implies an archaeological site (e.g. `Canyon Creek Ruin (Ariz.)`), and add a geographic qualifier, e.g. `Fengate Site (England)`, `Agate Basin Site (Wyo.)`. (H 1225 sec. F)
Sites within cities are qualified by the city name, e.g. `Young Site (Alton, Me.)`. (H 1225 sec. F; cf. H 810)

Site authority records get the broader term `[modern country]--Antiquities` (first-order political division for Canada, Great Britain, United States); farm/plantation sites also get `Farms--[modern country]` or `Plantations--[modern country]`. (H 1225 sec. F)
Remains of an extinct city are established as an extinct city (H 715), not as an archaeological site. (H 1225 sec. F)
A cemetery that is an archaeological site takes the word "Site" (H 405, Group 2). (H 1225 sec. F)

A named cave or mound site is established under the name of the cave or mound without the word "Site" (e.g. `Texcal Cave (Mexico)`, `Lewis Creek Mound (Va.)`), with BT `Caves--[modern country]` or `Mounds--[modern country]` plus `[modern country]--Antiquities`. (H 1225 sec. F)

sections.heading: A. Background
sections.text:
Works that discuss the archaeology of particular places are assigned a standard combination of subject headings. The purpose of this instruction sheet is to provide guidelines for assigning these headings to assure uniform treatment for such works.

LC practice: As stated in H 1075, LC catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT), e.g. *Catalogs*. To replace a form subdivision that includes a demographic group, also assign Library of Congress Demographic Groups Terms (LCDGT) to bring out the audience of the resource being cataloged, e.g. *German speakers* or *Arabic, Students of*.

sections.heading: B. Recent revisions
sections.text: 2026-07: Updated template. Added instructions related to LCGFT implementation.

sections.heading: C. Definitions
sections.text: Antiquities: Artifacts, relics, buildings, or monuments of the past, often associated with archaeological work.

sections.heading: D. General rule
sections.text:
To works on the archaeology of a particular place, assign an appropriate combination of the following headings, as specified in sec. D.1.-D.4., below.

Model:

```
651 #0 $a [name of site, if the work is about a specific site]
651 #0 $a [place] $x Antiquities <or Antiquities, Roman [etc.]
650 #0 $a Antiquities, Prehistoric $z [place]
650 #0 $a [name of people, prehistoric culture or period, etc.]
650 #0 $a Excavations (Archaeology) $z [place]
```

Also assign headings to bring out any other special topics, such as pottery, burial sites, agriculture, etc. Divide these headings by place, including the name of the site if the work is about an individual site.

sections.heading: D.1. Name of the site
sections.text: For works about a specific site, assign the heading for the site. For procedures for establishing headings for individual sites, see sec. F below.

sections.heading: D.2. Place--Antiquities and/or Antiquities, Prehistoric--Place
sections.text:
Assign a heading of the type *[place]--Antiquities* to works on the antiquities of a particular place, for example, *Africa--Antiquities*; *France--Antiquities*; *London (England)--Antiquities*.

If a work is about a specific site, assign this heading only to bring out a locality below the level of a country (or below the level of a first order political division in the case of the United States, Great Britain, and Canada).

Use the subdivision *--Antiquities, Byzantine, [Celtic, Germanic, Phoenician, Roman, Slavic, or Turkish]* if the work is about antiquities of one of those types. In all other cases, assign the subdivision *--Antiquities* without an adjectival qualifier.

For works on prehistoric antiquities, assign the heading *Antiquities, Prehistoric--[place]*. Do not divide this heading by names of individual sites.

sections.heading: D.3. Name of people
sections.text:
When possible, assign a heading for the people who occupied the site, or assign a heading for the prehistoric culture or period. Subdivide this heading geographically if appropriate. Under headings for extant peoples, use the subdivision *--Antiquities*.

Examples:

```
650 #0 $a Sumerians.
650 #0 $a Mesolithic period.
650 #0 $a Copper age $z Europe.
650 #0 $a Hallstatt period.
650 #0 $a Corded Ware culture.
650 #0 $a Neanderthals $z France $z Poitou-Charentes.
650 #0 $a Indus civilization.
650 #0 $a Calf Creek culture.
650 #0 $a Mayas $x Antiquities.
```

If the work is about two peoples, cultures, or periods, designate both. If it is about more than two, or if the name of the people, culture, or period cannot be identified from the work, this type of heading may be omitted.

Assign this heading even if the subdivision *--Antiquities* has been qualified by the name of the corresponding ethnic group. For example, in the following case, the heading Celts is required even though *--Antiquities, Celtic* has been used in the first heading:

Example:

```
651 #0 $a Romania $x Antiquities, Celtic.
650 #0 $a Celts $z Romania.
```

Exception: Do not assign the heading *Romans* if either *Italy--Antiquities, Roman* or *[locality within Italy]--Antiquities, Roman* has been assigned.

Do not assign this heading if the place used in the *[place]--Antiquities* heading corresponds exactly to the name of the people (for example, *Greece* and *Greeks*; *Egypt* and *Egyptians*; *Gaul* and *Gauls*; *Hawaii* and *Hawaiians*; *Rome* and *Romans*).

sections.heading: D.4. Excavations (Archaeology)--[place]
sections.text: Assign this heading if the work is about excavations carried out in the place, including techniques used, artifacts recovered, etc. Do not divide this heading by names of individual sites.

sections.heading: E. Catalogs of antiquities
sections.text:
Use the free-floating form subdivision *--Catalogs* under names of individual sites and under headings of the type *[place]--Antiquities* and *Excavations (Archaeology)--[place]* for works listing objects found at those sites.

Do not use *--Catalogs* under headings for peoples. For example, use *Rome--Antiquities--Catalogs*, not *Romans--Catalogs*.

LC practice: Assign a subject heading for all the categories listed in sec. D. If the work contains a list of the objects found at the site that is more than 20% of the resource, also assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand, e.g. LCGFT *Catalogs*.

sections.heading: F. Establishing names of individual sites
sections.text:
In general, follow the rules in H 690, Formulating Geographic Headings, for establishing archaeological sites. For those archaeological sites that are obscure and unlikely to be found in any standard reference sources, select the site name on the basis of the work being cataloged. Add the word "Site" to the name unless the name includes a term that implies an archaeological site, for example, *Canyon Creek Ruin (Ariz.)*. Add the appropriate geographic qualifier. Qualify headings for sites within cities by the name of the city (cf. H 810).

Examples:

```
151 ## $a Fengate Site (England)
151 ## $a Agate Basin Site (Wyo.)
151 ## $a Young Site (Alton, Me.)
```

Add the following reference(s) and broader term:

Model:

```
451 ## $a [alternate name(s)] ([geographic qualifier])
551 ## $w g $a [modern country] $x Antiquities
```

Note: In the above model, the term [modern country] refers, in the case of Canada, Great Britain, and the United States, to the first order political division.

If the site currently functions as a farm or plantation, also add the broader term *Farms--[modern country]* or *Plantations--[modern country]*.

If the site constitutes the remains of an extinct city, establish it as an extinct city rather than an archaeological site, following the provisions of H 715.

In the case of a cemetery that is an archaeological site, add the word "Site" to the name in accordance with H 405, Group 2.

If the site is a cave or mound site and the cave or mound has been named, establish the name of the cave or mound, omitting the word "Site". Add the broader term *Caves--[modern country]* or *Mounds--[modern country]* in addition to the references specified in the model above.

Examples:

```
151 ## $a Texcal Cave (Mexico)
550 ## $w $g $a Caves $z Mexico
551 ## $w $g $a Mexico $x Antiquities

151 ## $a Wise Rockshelter (Ohio)
550 ## $w $g $a Caves $z Ohio
551 ## $w $g $a Ohio $x Antiquities

151 ## $a Lewis Creek Mound (Va.)
550 ## $w $g $a Mounds $z Virginia
551 ## $w $g $a Virginia $x Antiquities
```

sections.heading: G. Extended examples
sections.text:
```
Title: Archaeological treasures of ancient Egypt.
651 #0 $a Egypt $x Antiquities.

Title: Etruscan painted tombs of Tarquinia, Italy.
651 #0 $a Tarquinia (Italy) $x Antiquities.
650 #0 $a Etruscans $z Italy $z Tarquinia.
650 #0 $a Tombs $z Italy $z Tarquinia.
650 #0 $a Mural painting and decoration, Etruscan $z Italy $z Tarquinia.

Title: Remains of Roman roads in Lombardy.
651 #0 $a Lombardy (Italy) $x Antiquities, Roman.
650 #0 $a Roads, Roman $z Italy $z Lombardy.

Title: Studies of Phoenician settlements in early Spain.
651 #0 $a Spain $x Antiquities, Phoenician.
650 #0 $a Phoenicians $z Spain.

Title: Archaeological excavations of Pueblo sites in Chaco Canyon, New Mexico.
651 #0 $a Chaco Canyon (N.M.) $x Antiquities.
650 #0 $a Pueblo Indians $x Antiquities.
650 #0 $a Excavations (Archaeology) $z New Mexico $z Chaco Canyon.

Title: Danebury, anatomy of an Iron Age hillfort.
651 #0 $a Danebury Site (England)
650 #0 $a Fortification, Prehistoric $z England #z Danebury Site.
650 #0 $a Iron age $z England $z Danebury Site.

Title: Selected early Mississippian household sites in the American Bottom.
650 #0 $a Indians of North America $z Illinois $z American Bottom $x Antiquities.
650 #0 $a Mississippian culture $z Illinois $z American Bottom.
650 #0 $a Excavations (Archaeology) $z Illinois $z American Bottom.
651 #0 $a American Bottom (Ill.) $x Antiquities.

Title: The Grand Village of the Natchez revisited : excavations at the Fatherland site, Adams County, Mississippi, 1972.
651 #0 $a Fatherland Site (Miss.)
650 #0 $a Natchez Indians $x Antiquities.
650 #0 $a Excavations (Archaeology) $z Mississippi $z Adams County.

Title: Archeology of Kauai.
651 #0 Kauai (Hawaii) $x Antiquities.
650 #0 $a Excavations (Archaeology) $z Hawaii $z Kauai.
```

(Examples copied as printed. Source typos: "#z Danebury Site" should be "$z Danebury Site"; "651 #0 Kauai" lacks "$a"; "$w $g" in the cave/mound examples corresponds to "$w g" in the model; the model line "<or Antiquities, Roman [etc.]" lacks a closing ">".)
